title: Duke Ellington at the Apollo: asked off the bill, later congratulating Slim and Slam
summary: Slim and Slam's first theater job was a bill with Ellington, who had them dropped as too weak; a year later they topped the Apollo bill and Ellington congratulated them.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, well, now, did you ever -- let me see. Could you tell us about some of your encounters with Duke Ellington?

Oh, yes. I had -- I think I mentioned a long time ago, when my parents took me over to New York to see the Duke at the Apollo Theater? Well, I met him for the first time that day when we went over, but it was a very brief meeting, you know. But anyway, that's when I -- that's before even TV and what have you. This goes back to, oh, 1935, something like that.
Yeah, you told me you were about 19.
That's right. It was a thrill for me to meet the great Duke Ellington. Of course, I had met Slim Gaillard -- of course, I had been playing with Slim and --
This was later, after --
That was a little later, yeah.
Right.
And here's what I want to say. Let's say two, three years later after I had met him, Slim and I played the Apollo, the same theater that I went to see him,

where I first met Duke, and of course, Slim and I was on the bill with Duke Ellington and his band. We did our thing, of course, and Duke had his band there and of course, he had the top billing. He was the thing. And Slim was -- this was Slim and my first exposure in a theater after we got together.
Oh, this was your first theater gig.

First theater gig. And that was the Apollo Theater. So anyway, after we did our thing, the very first show, Slim and I, we did our thing, somehow the manager called us up to his office and told Slim and myself that our act wasn't too good. "As a matter of fact, Mr. Ellington would request that you all not finish this week's engagement because your act isn't strong enough to fit this particular show and it might hurt the Duke Ellington performance for that week." That's what Duke had said about Slim and myself.
This was your -- how long had you all been working together? Had you all just started working together then?
We had just started more or less.
Uh-huh. Now did he later change his mind?

Well, now, here's what happened. We finished that first day and said, "Okay, what I mean, Duke doesn't want us to play on the show with him, so well, we'll just forget it. The hell with it," you know. "The H with it."
(Laughter.)

So anyway, about a year passed. Slim and I went back into the Apollo Theater with our own names, with our names topping the bill, and we did so great that we got a letter of congratulations from Duke Ellington and he came by to see us and he didn't exactly apologize to us, but he came by and you could see that he wanted to tell us that he was sorry for what he did the year before, you know, when we were on his show. So I thought that was nice, you know.
Yeah, I guess he had a lot more -- a lot of guys in his position who did that wouldn't have --
That's right.
They'd have had too much ego to --
Yeah. No, he said that we weren't strong enough for that particular show.
Do you think that, in fact, a year later, that -- well, it must have been stronger a year later anyway, if you played --
Oh, yes, sure.
Yeah.

Now I don't know if we were suitable at that time for that particular show that we did with Duke Ellington, you know. But anyway, we paid it no mind, you know, just youngsters coming up. So we did the best we could and under the circumstances, we did great when we returned to the Apollo Theater.
